## 1. Load Libraries

```{r libraries}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(DBI)
library(odbc)
library(keyring)
library(purrr)
library(writexl)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. Connect to LIMS and Pull Data

```{r lims-connect}
con <- dbConnect(
  odbc(),
  Driver                = "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server",
  Server                = "DOH01DBTUMP22,9799",
  Database              = "LIMS_DATA",
  TrustServerCertificate = "Yes",
  Trusted_Connection    = "Yes"
)

lims_data <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT * FROM [vz_Epi_ELS_Multiplex_SARS-Flu-RSV-Mpox_dPCR]"
)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Import and Combine Run Stats Excel File

```{r import-excel}
# Set file path (update as needed)
file_path <- "/mnt/c/Users/qxy0303/scratch/WAWBE_outcome_analysis/Run Stats.xlsx"

# Read all sheets and append with sheet name as IC_Group
sheets <- excel_sheets(file_path)

df <- lapply(sheets, function(sheet_name) {
  read_excel(file_path, sheet = sheet_name) %>%
    mutate(IC_Group = sheet_name)
}) %>%
  bind_rows()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Clean and Merge Data

```{r clean-merge}
# Rename columns
colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "Key_ID"]        <- "PHLAccessionNumber"
colnames(df)[colnames(df) == ">10X Coverage"] <- "Coverage_10X"

# Merge WWTP names from LIMS
df <- merge(
  df,
  lims_data[, c("PHLAccessionNumber", "WWTPName")],
  by = "PHLAccessionNumber"
)

# Drop unneeded columns
df <- df %>%
  select(-all_of(c(
    "0x Coverage",
    "...10",
    "...11",
    "#A",
    "#B",
    "#A/B",
    "#C",
    "% Failed",
    "% PASS (A)",
    "% PASS (A/B)",
    "Column1",
    "Library Prep Input Copies"
  )))

# Remove all-NA rows and the validation table sheet
df <- df %>%
  filter(
    rowSums(is.na(.)) != ncol(.),
    IC_Group != "Val Table"
  )

# Duplicated rows after merging, remove dups by WA# - QY
df <- df[!duplicated(df), ]


glimpse(df)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Correlation: Input Copies vs. \>10X Coverage

```{r correlation}
cor_result <- cor.test(
  df$`Input Copies`,
  df$Coverage_10X,
  method = "pearson"
)

cor_result
```

> **Pearson r = `r round(cor_result$estimate, 3)`**, p = `r signif(cor_result$p.value, 3)`

### Scatter Plot

```{r scatter-plot}
ggplot(df, aes(x = `Input Copies`, y = Coverage_10X)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, color = "red", linewidth = 1.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 200)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 90, 100)) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Between Concentration and >10X Coverage",
    x     = "Number of Input Copies",
    y     = "Samples with >10X Coverage"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 6. WWTP-Level Boxplots

```{r wwtp-label-fn}
# Shared label-cleaning function for WWTP names
clean_wwtp <- function(x) {
  gsub(
    "WWTP|Water|Reclamation|Facility|Treatment|Plant|Wastewater|WRP|Clean|\\(SCTP\\)|Influent|Regional|and|Sewage",
    "", x
  )
}
```

### Input Copies by WWTP

```{r boxplot-input-copies}
ggplot(df, aes(x = WWTPName, y = `Input Copies`, fill = WWTPName)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 200)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = clean_wwtp) +
  labs(title = "Input Copies by WWTP", x = NULL, y = "Input Copies") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```

### Samples with \>10X Coverage by WWTP

```{r boxplot-10x-coverage}
ggplot(df, aes(x = WWTPName, y = Coverage_10X, fill = WWTPName)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = clean_wwtp) +
  labs(title = "Samples with >10X Coverage by WWTP", x = NULL, y = ">10X Coverage (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```

## 7. Quality Summary Table by WWTP

![](images/clipboard-4020351230.png)

```{r quality-summary}
quality_summary <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Quality = case_when(
      Coverage_10X >= 90                          ~ "A",
      Coverage_10X >= 60 & Coverage_10X < 90      ~ "B",
      Coverage_10X < 60                           ~ "Fail",
      TRUE                                        ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(WWTPName) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Samples    = n(),
    Percent_A        = round(mean(Quality == "A",    na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
    Percent_B        = round(mean(Quality == "B",    na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
    Percent_Fail     = round(mean(Quality == "Fail", na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
    Avg_Input_Copies = round(mean(`Input Copies`,    na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Percent_A))

quality_summary
```

```{r write-quality-summary, eval=FALSE}
# Export (run manually as needed)
write.csv(quality_summary, file = "WWTP_by_Sample_Quality.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write_xlsx(quality_summary, "quality_summary.xlsx")
```

## 8. IC Group × QCD Pivot Table

```{r ic-group-pivot}
df2 <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(QCD)) %>%
  mutate(
    IC_Group = case_when(
      `Input Copies` >= 0   & `Input Copies` <= 4.9    ~ "IC 0-4",
      `Input Copies` >= 5   & `Input Copies` <= 9.9    ~ "IC 5-9",
      `Input Copies` >= 10  & `Input Copies` <= 19.9   ~ "IC 10-19",
      `Input Copies` >= 20  & `Input Copies` <= 29.9   ~ "IC 20-29",
      `Input Copies` >= 30  & `Input Copies` <= 39.9   ~ "IC 30-39",
      `Input Copies` >= 40  & `Input Copies` <= 49.9   ~ "IC 40-49",
      `Input Copies` >= 50  & `Input Copies` <= 100.9  ~ "IC 50-100",
      `Input Copies` >= 101 & `Input Copies` <= 1000   ~ "IC 101-1000",
      TRUE                                             ~ "Other"
    )
  )

IC_Group_Table <- df2 %>%
  group_by(WWTPName, IC_Group, QCD) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = c(IC_Group, QCD),
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )

IC_Group_Table
```

```{r write-ic-group, eval=FALSE}
# Export (run manually as needed)
write.csv(df2, "WWTP_QCD_Data_2.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## 9. Multiple Linear Regression

This might be the most straightfoward method to figure out the main contributing factor in the sequencing outcome. This might require subsetting samples and focus on the samples with low input copies to identify variables contributing to sequencing outcome variation.

In addition, categorical data such as WWTP names, needs to be factorized so that lm() function will convert it to dummy variables automatically.

```{r MLR}
library(ggcorrplot)


# Convert categorical data to numeric and factors
df$WWTPName <- as.factor(df$WWTPName)

# Focus on only sample with low input copies
reduced_data <- subset(df, `Input Copies`<=40)
# reduced_data <- subset(df, `Input Copies`>=0)

# Remove the irrelevant columns
reduced_data <- subset(reduced_data, select = -c(PHLAccessionNumber, QCD, IC_Group))

# Compute correlation between variables, only works for quantitative variables
corr_matrix = cor(subset(reduced_data, select = -c(WWTPName)), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Compute and show the  result
ggcorrplot(corr_matrix, hc.order = TRUE, type = "lower", lab = TRUE)
```

Refine model by removing inter-correlating variables, then construct the linear model

```{r}
# Fit a multiple linear regression model
cov10x_model = lm(formula = Coverage_10X ~ 
                    `Input Copies` + 
                    Library_Concetration + 
                    `Total Reads` + 
                    Coverage + 
                    WWTPName,
                  data = reduced_data)

# Plot the model residuals to ensure normality of residual distribution
hist(cov10x_model$residuals)
```

The summarized coefficient and p-value give an estimate of whether a sample is significantly and positively/negatively correlating with sequencing outcomes.

```{r}
summary(cov10x_model)
```

## 10. Principle component analysis

This might help visually separate out data points through dimentionality reduction. Might also be helpful to use interactive ploting tool to overlay additional metadata.

```{r}
library(plotly)

# Convert factorized categorical data to dummy variables
reduced_data_num <- model.matrix(~ . - 1, data = reduced_data)
# Compute PCA
pca_res <- prcomp(reduced_data_num, scale. = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Extract %variance expained by each component
explained_variance_ratio <- summary(pca_res)[["importance"]]['Proportion of Variance',]
explained_variance_ratio <- 100 * explained_variance_ratio


# Merge metadata with the PCA data
pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x)
pca_data <- merge(pca_data, reduced_data, by = "row.names")
```

```{r}
# Convert categorical string labels to a numeric factor for coloring
wwtp_numeric <- as.numeric(pca_data$WWTPName)

# Axis configuration
axis_cfg = list(showline = TRUE,
                gridcolor = '#ffff',
                ticklen = 4,
                titlefont = list(size = 13))

# Plot PC components in splom chart
fig <- plot_ly(data = pca_data) %>%
  add_trace(
    type = 'splom',
    dimensions = list(
      list(label = paste('PC 1 (', round(explained_variance_ratio[1], 1), '%)', sep = ''), values = ~PC1),
      list(label = paste('PC 2 (', round(explained_variance_ratio[2], 1), '%)', sep = ''), values = ~PC2),
      list(label = paste('PC 3 (', round(explained_variance_ratio[3], 1), '%)', sep = ''), values = ~PC3),
      list(label = paste('PC 4 (', round(explained_variance_ratio[4], 1), '%)', sep = ''), values = ~PC4)
    ),
    # Pre-configure the trace container marker settings cleanly
    marker = list(
      color = pca_data$Coverage_10X,
      colorscale = 'Viridis',
      showscale = TRUE,
      cmin = min(pca_data$Coverage_10X, na.rm = TRUE),
      cmax = max(pca_data$Coverage_10X, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  ) %>%
  style(diagonal = list(visible = FALSE)) %>%
  layout(
    legend = list(title = list(text = 'color')),
    hovermode = 'closest',
    dragmode = 'select',
    xaxis = axis_cfg, yaxis = axis_cfg,
    xaxis2 = axis_cfg, xaxis3 = axis_cfg, xaxis4 = axis_cfg,
    yaxis2 = axis_cfg, yaxis3 = axis_cfg, yaxis4 = axis_cfg
  )


# Add dropdown menu
fig <- fig %>% layout(
  updatemenus = list(
    list(
      y = 0.8,
      type = "dropdown",
      buttons = list(
        # Button 1: Coverage 10X
        list(
          method = "restyle",
          args = list(
            list(
              "marker.color" = list(pca_data$Coverage_10X),
              "marker.cmin" = min(pca_data$Coverage_10X, na.rm = TRUE),
              "marker.cmax" = max(pca_data$Coverage_10X, na.rm = TRUE)
            )
          ),
          label = "Coverage 10X"
        ),
        # Button 2: WWTP Names
        list(
          method = "restyle",
          args = list(
            list(
              "marker.color" = list(wwtp_numeric),
              "marker.cmin" = min(wwtp_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
              "marker.cmax" = max(wwtp_numeric, na.rm = TRUE)
            )
          ),
          label = "WWTP Names"
        ),
        # Button 3: Input Copies
        list(
          method = "restyle",
          args = list(
            list(
              "marker.color" = list(pca_data$`Input Copies`),
              "marker.cmin" = min(pca_data$`Input Copies`, na.rm = TRUE),
              "marker.cmax" = max(pca_data$`Input Copies`, na.rm = TRUE)
            )
          ),
          label = "Input Copies"
        )
      )
    )
  )
)

fig
```
